# EKS inference: eight checked configuration bundles

<!-- Generated by npm run certified-bundles. Do not edit by hand. -->

This example shows how one inference platform is assembled from eight separate configuration bundles. Start here to understand the configuration without creating an EKS cluster or paying for a GPU.

The packages below were read from GHCR on 2026-08-20T19:03:35Z. Every extracted file matched [the producer's committed configuration](https://github.com/confighub/eks-inference/blob/f6a1689c2fe231d1bc2262d9916aa69a774882b4/components.yaml) at commit [f6a1689c2fe2](https://github.com/confighub/eks-inference/commit/f6a1689c2fe231d1bc2262d9916aa69a774882b4).

## What runs where

| Plane | Order | Component | Purpose | Source | Extra handling |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ConfigHub only | 0 | [platform-profile](./receipts/eks-inference/platform-profile/receipt.yaml) | Shared values used by the other components; stored in ConfigHub and never applied to a cluster. | Literal YAML | None recorded |
| Management cluster | 0 | [ack-controllers](./receipts/eks-inference/ack-controllers/receipt.yaml) | ACK EC2, IAM, and EKS controllers and their CRDs. | Helm render | [crd-ordering](./routes/eks-inference/ack-controllers/crd-ordering.yaml) |
| Management cluster | 1 | [aws-network](./receipts/eks-inference/aws-network/receipt.yaml) | VPC, subnets, NAT, route tables, and security group. | Literal YAML | None recorded |
| Management cluster | 2 | [eks-cluster](./receipts/eks-inference/eks-cluster/receipt.yaml) | Cluster and node IAM roles, EKS control plane, addons, and system node group. | Literal YAML | None recorded |
| Management cluster | 3 | [karpenter-aws](./receipts/eks-inference/karpenter-aws/receipt.yaml) | Karpenter controller IAM role and EKS Pod Identity association. | Literal YAML | None recorded |
| EKS workload cluster | 0 | [karpenter](./receipts/eks-inference/karpenter/receipt.yaml) | Karpenter CRDs, controller, NodePools, and EC2NodeClasses. | Helm render | [crd-ordering](./routes/eks-inference/karpenter/crd-ordering.yaml) |
| EKS workload cluster | 1 | [gpu-runtime](./receipts/eks-inference/gpu-runtime/receipt.yaml) | NVIDIA device plugin, so GPU nodes advertise their hardware. | Helm render | None recorded |
| EKS workload cluster | 2 | [inference-workloads](./receipts/eks-inference/inference-workloads/receipt.yaml) | CPU and GPU checks, a chat client, and the sample vLLM deployment. | Literal YAML | None recorded |

The `platform-profile` is shared data, not a deployable workload. The management cluster runs ACK and creates the AWS network, EKS cluster, and Karpenter identity. Only after EKS is active does the workload cluster run Karpenter, the GPU plugin, and the inference workloads. Ordering inside one bundle does not order these separate planes; the `cub eksinf` workflow waits between them.

## Inspect the configuration first

The receipts, routes, and public OCI packages can be inspected without a ConfigHub account. For example:

```sh
oras pull ghcr.io/confighub/configs/eks-inference/inference-workloads@sha256:4ae5737725c86f7a07cf3366a7eafee8625a0dd8487784aa581ce7e33d460eb2
```

## Build the configuration in ConfigHub

```sh
cub plugin install confighub/eks-inference
cub eksinf install
cub eksinf sandbox up
```

This path requires a ConfigHub account, but no AWS account, Docker, Kubernetes cluster, or GPU. It creates the component bases and sandbox variants, links their shared values, runs the ConfigHub checks, and publishes releases. No controller consumes those releases, so it proves the configuration path rather than a deployment.

Config Workshop independently checked this sandbox on 2026-08-20T19:26:07.326Z. The live ConfigHub organization held all eight source digests, eight linked variants, 27 configured destination fields, two OCI sandbox targets, and seven published Releases. [Read the proof](../eks-inference-sandbox-proof/summary.md).

That proof stops at published OCI. It does not claim that Argo CD or Flux pulled a Release, AWS resources were created, a GPU became ready, or a model answered a request.

## Change, promote, and deliver one configuration

A separate live test changed only `apps/v1 Deployment inference/chat spec.replicas` from 1 to 2. ConfigHub retained that change in dev, promoted the same five Unit hashes to staging, published the result as OCI, and Argo CD pulled the exact Release manifest digest. Kubernetes then reported 2/2 chat replicas available. [Read the promotion and delivery proof](../eks-inference-promotion-delivery-proof/summary.md).

The GPU check and vLLM configuration remained at zero replicas. This proves one small configuration promotion and Argo delivery on a local cluster, not AWS provisioning, GPU readiness, or a model response.

## What this evidence does not prove

Matching OCI bytes do not prove that ConfigHub created the sandbox, ACK provisioned AWS, EKS became ready, a GPU node started, or vLLM answered a request. Those are separate lifecycle and runtime results. They need separate receipts from the exact target.

[Follow the producer's current walkthrough](https://github.com/confighub/eks-inference/tree/f6a1689c2fe231d1bc2262d9916aa69a774882b4) when you are ready for the real AWS and GPU path.
